title: So you've heard these AI terms and nodded along; let's fix that
description: Comprehensive glossary explaining common AI terminology including concepts like hallucinations, tokens, fine-tuning, RAG (retrieval-augmented generation), and other jargon that has emerged with the rise of large language models. The article serves as an educational resource for developers and non-technical readers trying to navigate AI discourse.
author: TechCrunch Staff

title: Notes on WebRTC prompt degradation
description: Technical critique of WebRTC's aggressive packet dropping behavior during poor network conditions. Willison argues that for expensive LLM prompts, users would prefer higher latency over accuracy loss, but WebRTC's hard-coded implementation prevents waiting or retransmission. This highlights infrastructure challenges in voice-based AI interactions.
author: Simon Willison

title: PlayStation sees AI as a 'powerful tool' to help make games
description: Sony's PlayStation division is actively integrating AI-powered animation tools into game development studios, with Naughty Dog and Santa Monica Studio already adopting the technology. This reflects the growing trend of major game studios using AI to streamline workflows and improve development efficiency.
author: Jay Peters

title: Using Claude Code: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of HTML
description: Simon Willison explores Thariq Shihipar's argument for requesting HTML output from Claude instead of Markdown. While Markdown was previously preferred for token efficiency, HTML enables richer outputs including SVG diagrams, interactive widgets, and in-page navigation. Willison demonstrates this by having GPT-5.5 create an interactive HTML explanation of the copy.fail Linux security exploit, showing how HTML format allows for more comprehensive and navigable technical documentation.
author: Simon Willison

title: Nanoleaf bets its future on robots, red light therapy, and AI
description: Smart lighting company Nanoleaf is pivoting beyond its core business to invest in robotics and AI-powered products. CEO Gimmy Chu explains that commoditization of smart lighting is driving the company's strategic shift toward AI-driven home automation and robotic solutions.
author: Jennifer Pattison Tuohy

title: Databricks Has a Trick That Lets AI Models Improve Themselves
description: Databricks has developed a technique enabling AI models to improve their own performance without requiring extensive human labeling or retraining. The approach leverages synthetic data generation and self-evaluation mechanisms, potentially reducing the cost and time required to enhance model accuracy and capabilities.
author: Will Knight

title: The battle over AI data centers
description: Comprehensive analysis of the growing infrastructure demands of AI development, examining the race to build specialized data centers capable of training and deploying massive AI models. The coverage explores energy consumption, geographic distribution, and the geopolitical implications of AI computing infrastructure.
author: Verge Staff and Justine Calma

title: OpenAI launched a Codex extension for Chrome
description: OpenAI has released a Chrome extension for Codex that allows it to use Chrome on your computer to complete work inside websites and apps where you're already signed in. The extension works in task-specific tab groups, enabling developers to maintain productivity while automating workflows across multiple web applications.
author: Jay Peters

title: Behind the Scenes Hardening Firefox with Claude Mythos Preview
description: Coverage of Mozilla's use of Claude Mythos preview to identify and fix security vulnerabilities in Firefox. The article details how AI-generated security bug reports evolved from mostly unwanted 'slop' to high-quality findings, with Mozilla fixing 423 security bugs in April 2026 (up from 20-30 per month throughout 2025). This demonstrates a major advancement in AI-assisted security research.
author: Simon Willison

title: Gmail's 'Help me write' AI tool will draft emails that sound more like you
description: Google is rolling out an update to Gmail's 'Help me write' AI feature that generates emails personalized to your tone and writing style. The tool can now pull in relevant context from Google Drive and Gmail history, making AI-generated communications more authentic and contextually relevant.
author: Jay Peters

title: Mozilla is sharing more details about some of the 271 Firefox bugs identified by Claude Mythos Preview
description: Mozilla revealed that Anthropic's Claude Mythos Preview model helped identify 271 bugs in Firefox. Breaking from their usual practice of keeping bug reports private for months, Mozilla decided to publicly release details of some bug reports due to the extraordinary level of interest and urgency in AI-assisted security research.
author: Jay Peters

title: Cloudflare is laying off 1,100 workers as its AI usage increases by 600 percent
description: Cloudflare announced it's reducing its workforce by 1,100 employees while reporting a 600% increase in AI usage. The company stated these actions are about redefining how a high-growth company operates in the 'agentic AI era,' highlighting how AI automation is transforming workforce dynamics even at tech companies scaling their AI capabilities.
author: Emma Roth

title: Anthropic Launches the World's First 'Hybrid Reasoning' AI Model
description: Anthropic has unveiled what it claims is the first 'hybrid reasoning' AI model, combining different types of reasoning approaches to improve performance on complex tasks. The model represents an evolution in AI architecture that could impact how developers approach building AI-powered applications requiring sophisticated logical reasoning.
author: Will Knight

title: Vibe coding and agentic engineering are getting closer than I'd like
description: Simon Willison discusses how the distinction between 'vibe coding' (non-programmers using AI to build tools without understanding code) and 'agentic engineering' (professional software engineers using AI tools responsibly) is beginning to blur. He expresses concern about not reviewing every line of code that AI agents write, even for production systems, and compares trusting AI agents to trusting software built by other teams. Key insight: as coding agents become more reliable, engineers face the challenge of evaluating software quality when superficial indicators like commit counts and documentation can now be generated quickly by AI.
author: Simon Willison

title: AI evaluation startup Braintrust confirms breach, tells every customer to rotate sensitive keys
description: AI evaluation platform Braintrust confirmed a security breach and has advised all customers to rotate their sensitive API keys and credentials. The incident highlights growing security concerns around AI developer tools that store and process sensitive authentication data for multiple AI services.
author: Lorenzo Franceschi-Bicchierai

title: Snap says its relationship with Perplexity ended 'amicably'
description: Snap ended its AI search partnership with Perplexity, noting in its Q1 2026 investor letter that analysts should not expect any contribution from Perplexity in revenue guidance. The AI search engine was originally intended to power Snap's AI features, but the company remains committed to 'intelligent eyewear' with more Specs news expected in June.
author: Victoria Song

title: Boston Dynamics Led a Robot Revolution. Now Its Machines Are Teaching Themselves New Tricks
description: Boston Dynamics is transitioning from pre-programmed robot behaviors to machine learning approaches that enable robots to learn new skills autonomously. The shift represents a fundamental change in robotics development, moving away from hand-coded control systems toward AI-driven learning and adaptation.
author: Will Knight

title: Live blog: Code w/ Claude 2026
description: Simon Willison provided live coverage of Anthropic's Code w/ Claude event, including morning keynote sessions. This appears to be part of Anthropic's developer-focused event showcasing Claude's coding capabilities.
author: Simon Willison

title: Granite 4.1 3B SVG Pelican Gallery experiment
description: Simon Willison tested IBM's Granite 4.1 family of LLMs (Apache 2.0 licensed in 3B, 8B, and 30B sizes) by prompting different quantized variants to generate an SVG of a pelican riding a bicycle. The results showed no clear correlation between model size and output quality, with all variants producing poor results. This provides insight into current limitations of LLM visual generation capabilities.
author: Simon Willison
